- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–4% for the next 3–7 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >75), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise; cap forecast at +2% above peak for next 5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of high prices followed by sharp drop), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong volatility, model is lagging; add 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (or vice versa), model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment change within 2–3 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating upward bias; increase forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5 days.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model is overestimating downward bias; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5 days.
